interactions.title: Leaving the Te’kula refuge
lines: DM: Okay, so we will start this little prequel as you leave the village of the Te'kula following Theba and your friends from the dream world that that Deno'qai tribe had been hiding in, back to the material world, and as the—that fabric of the dream space of the pocket dimension collapses around you as you leave, you're aware of the strangeness of the forest, of the many places you've journeyed and the many places, ah, you have yet to see.

after: DM: And really, you slap your hand on Baxter's shoulder. Yeah, the infinite possible adventures that spiral out from this, um, moment almost, ah, appear before you like seeds floating on the wind.

DM: And as you walk the world slowly fades around you until you're pulled back to your friends suddenly in a jumbled collection of images as the pocket dimension collapses: a meadow of golden butterflies, a forest of pines and maples high on a mountain slope, a dense tropical forest.

DM: As you feel Delwath, Kenzo and Seeker pulled away from you, you quickly reach into each of their minds in turn, just for a moment, shouting, “Find your way to the Feywild. The portal near Eudomes' tower. We'll meet there again.”

DM: And then you are hurtling towards the open ocean in the late afternoon light. The sun may be a few hours from setting across the ocean behind you. In the clear blue waters below, you see two ships. One, running before the westerly winds, is recognizably halfling, triple-masted and under full sail, the bright colors of the sails shining in the sun, although damage to the top sails suggests a recent engagement.

DM: Chasing it, a few miles behind, but gaining quickly, is a sleek warship, a huge ballista mounted on its bow. Well, it's too far in the distance from this vantage point for you to make out any particular details. The flag flying from the tallest mast, depicting a skull cleaved in two by a massive axe, cannot be a good sign.

Where are we? Who are they?”
DM: She looks— She looks surprised and confused, but also like she doesn't really have time to think about anything that you just said at the moment.
DM: “We're about a day's sail east of the Devil's Spine.”
DM: She says, “Those damn Skullcleaver hobgoblins got the better of us. We can just hold out for dark, I'm sure we can give them the slip.” She looks back, and— them.
DM: “Don’t have time to shepherd new sailors right now. Let's talk about it after— if you know how to sail.”
Wellby: Yeah, I spent the first ten years of my life between Tollen and Sembara, up and down the Green Sea.
DM: Are way to the west.
DM: That's way to the west.
Wellby: Um, all right, all right. This is extremely exciting. Wow! Okay.
DM: Ah, exciting is not the word I would use. We've got a cargo of dragonhide from Praznitsky, and if they catch us, it's done for.
Wellby: I don't know what any of those words mean. But 'catch us, I'm done for' makes sense. How can I help?
DM: Well, what can you do?
Wellby: Well, I can ride. This is Baxter, but I don't think that's going to help much.
Wellby: I can fight. I'm one of the best archers you've probably ever met. I can hide. I can make my way through the wilderness. Again, not super helpful in this context. I can scout. I can— we—
DM: Uh, she—she yells, “Pearl!” A stout like, buff, tall for a halfling woman comes over, wearing leather armor, a rapier at her side. She had been watching the trailing ship from the stern.
DM: “This guy dropped out of the sky, says he, he can fight. You can use him.”
DM: She says, “Sure, ah, hopefully, it won't come to that. But yeah, come with us.”

DM: She looks up. She looks at the sky, um. The older woman, the captain, looks at the wind.

DM: I mean, if you've got any ideas for how to slow them down, it certainly wouldn't hurt. We've got maybe three hours to darkness. I know these waters better than anybody. We just need to last that long.

lines: Wellby: Um, And then yeah, I'll say, uh, you know, to—to the first mate, I'll— is there anything that I should know about these ships? Like, is everyone carrying bows on them? What—what should I expect if I'm flying over it?

DM: They've lived in Wahacha a long time. The Vermillion Isles, we call them. It's a group of four or five islands that tend to cluster together, always can be found in close proximity to each other. Beautiful red stone cliffs stretching off from the blue ocean.

DM: I don't know how much you know of kenku. They say most of their people were slaves for many years far in the north to Cha'mutte, but the kenku of Wahacha descend from a different branch, a different lineage.

DM: Many of them have the white feathers and bright beaks reminiscent of seabirds, and they have lived in the East for millennia, I guess, since the Downfall, since the fall of Hkar and the upheaval of the land.

DM: I guess I would say they are— well, they— they don't build their cities in a way that is easy for grounders, as they call us, to navigate, perched up on the cliffs and high towers, but they are friendly enough as it goes.

DM: Some of them who I've spoken to know the Eastern Isles better than almost anyone. They travel widely.
